narrative.summary: South Africa has no AI-specific law: section 71 of the Protection of Personal Information Act on automated decision-making is the main binding rule. National AI policy rests on the communications department's August 2024 National AI Policy Framework; a Cabinet-approved Draft National AI Policy was published for comment in April 2026 and withdrawn in its entirety in June 2026. The financial sector regulators (FSCA and the Prudential Authority) published the first sector report on AI in 2025, and the 2020 Presidential Commission on the Fourth Industrial Revolution report remains a reference.
lead_institutions: Department of Communications and Digital Technologies
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The 2024 AI Policy Framework could only be located because the department's website was down, and the 2026 draft AI policy is shown as withdrawn.

instruments.official_title: Protection of Personal Information Act, 2013 (Act No. 4 of 2013)
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of the Republic of South Africa (assented to by the President; published by The Presidency, Government Notice 912, Government Gazette No. 37067)
instruments.current_status: In force (commenced in stages by presidential proclamation; the commencement dates are not stated in the Act as published and were not checked against the proclamations in this review). The Information Regulator established under the Act enforces it.
instruments.summary: South Africa's general data protection law: it sets eight conditions for lawful processing of personal information, regulates direct marketing, transborder flows and special personal information, and establishes the Information Regulator. Section 71 provides that a data subject may not be subject to a decision with legal consequences or substantial effect based solely on automated processing intended to profile the person (e.g. work performance, creditworthiness, health, conduct), unless the decision is linked to a contract with appropriate safeguards or governed by a law or code with such measures; the safeguards must let the person make representations and give sufficient information about the underlying logic of the processing.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rules on automated decision-making and profiling (s.71) and on personal data used to train and run AI systems; the main binding AI-relevant law in South Africa.

instruments.issuing_authority: Presidential Commission on the Fourth Industrial Revolution; published by the Minister of Communications and Digital Technologies (General Notice 591, Government Gazette No. 43834)
instruments.current_status: Published for general information in Government Gazette No. 43834 of 23 October 2020. Its recommendations underlie later AI work (the Draft National AI Policy of 2026 builds on the 2024 AI Policy Framework, which followed this report). Not a binding instrument.
instruments.summary: Report of the Presidential Commission on the 4th Industrial Revolution, published by the Minister of Communications and Digital Technologies under the Commission's terms of reference (Gazette No. 42388 of 9 April 2019). It diagnoses South Africa's readiness for 4IR technologies, including artificial intelligence, and makes key recommendations such as investing in human capacity, building digital infrastructure, establishing an AI institute (a 'creative AI, Big Data Analytics, Blockchain and Cybersecurity' institute), securing government and citizens' data and updating regulation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First government-commissioned national roadmap that framed AI as a priority and recommended an AI institute; precursor to the national AI policy process.

instruments.official_title: Draft South Africa National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy
instruments.english_title: Draft South Africa National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy (General Notice 3880 of 2026)
instruments.issuing_authority: Minister of Communications and Digital Technologies (Department of Communications and Digital Technologies); approved by Cabinet on 25 March 2026
instruments.current_status: Published for 60 days' public comment (deadline 10 June 2026) in Government Gazette No. 54477 of 10 April 2026 (notice signed 9 April 2026). Withdrawn in its entirety by the Minister through General Notice 3978 of 2026 (Gazette No. 54840, 12 June 2026; signed 4 June 2026), effective from the date of publication. The withdrawal notice states no reason. No replacement draft was found on official sites as of 2026-10-12.
instruments.summary: Cabinet-approved draft national AI policy published by the Minister of Communications and Digital Technologies for public comment under section 85(2)(b) of the Constitution. It set out strategic pillars and a staged implementation (finalise the policy and draft rules for unacceptable risks in 2025/26; guidelines and high-risk requirements in 2026/27) and proposed new institutions including a National AI Commission/Office, an AI Ethics Board, an AI Regulatory Authority, an AI Ombudsperson Office, an AI Insurance Superfund and a National AI Safety Institute, with ICASA repositioned and a National AI Regulatory Forum coordinating the Information Regulator, Competition Commission, SARB, FSCA and others. It was withdrawn before finalisation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: South Africa's first gazetted national AI policy draft; withdrawn, kept for the timeline.

instruments.official_title: Artificial Intelligence in the South African Financial Sector
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence in the South African Financial Sector
instruments.issuing_authority: Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) and Prudential Authority (PA, South African Reserve Bank)
instruments.current_status: Published jointly on 24 November 2025 (date of the FSCA/PA press release; the report cover says November 2025) on the SARB Prudential Authority publications page, with a databook and survey questionnaire. Non-binding; it envisages future sector-wide guidance on ethical and responsible AI.
instruments.summary: Joint FSCA and Prudential Authority report giving the first overview of AI, machine learning and generative AI adoption in South African financial institutions, based on a 2024 survey of banks, insurers, investment managers and payment providers. It reviews international regulatory approaches, use cases, risks (privacy, bias, explainability, systemic risk) and governance and ethics considerations, and sets out lessons: explainability methods, board-level AI governance and model risk management, disclosure of AI in consumer-impacting decisions such as credit and insurance pricing, coordination with the Information Regulator on POPIA, and planned sector-wide guidance.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Financial supervisors' first AI-specific publication and signal of forthcoming sector guidance.
